agent_notes: The superscription לְדָוִד is part of Hebrew verse 1 (KJV counts it as 26:0), so it is glossed and rendered here. 'Of David' is left open between author, dedicatee and Davidic collection; I did not decide it.

שָׁפְטֵנִי: KJV 'Judge me' and BBE 'be my judge' keep the neutral verb; YLT is also neutral. STEPBible 'vindicate me' is a fair reading of the context, but the verb itself is 'judge', and the next clause shows the speaker expects acquittal. I kept 'judge me' in the gloss and let the commentary carry the nuance. Rashi and Radak (via the midrash) put this in tension with Ps 143:2.

history.note: [consider] Consider 'Of David.' in the dramatic layer, and auditing the KJV's added 'A Psalm' rather than its 'also'. (PS.26.1: "לְדָוִד"; "וּבַיהוָה בָּטַחְתִּי"; Webster marks the KJV addition: "[A Psalm] of David".)

agent_notes: זִמָּה: Rashi says every occurrence in the Bible means 'plan', good or bad; Radak reads it as an abomination, a deed. The five English versions split between 'mischief', 'wickedness' and 'evil designs'. I chose 'scheme' in the literal layer to keep both the plotting and the hand that carries it out, and flagged the split in the note.

history.note: [consider] Consider 'Redeem me and be gracious to me' without 'LORD', and 'ten verses' in the commentary. (PS.26.11: "וַאֲנִי בְּתֻמִּי אֵלֵךְ פְּדֵנִי וְחָנֵּנִי" (no יְהוָה).)

agent_notes: Targum reads 'in the assembly of the righteous', which is not in the Hebrew בְּמַקְהֵלִים, a plural with no qualifier. I did not use that gloss.

Qere/Ketiv: the packet reads צָרְפָה (Qere); Radak notes the written form has an extra ו (צרופה, 'refined' as an adjective). I glossed the Qere imperative and mention the Ketiv in the note. The Ketiv would make 'my kidneys and my heart are refined', as YLT reads it, so the choice changes the sense from a plea to a claim.

Root of מְתֵי corrected to מת (H4962, 'man', plural construct), as the reviewer asked; the note reads 'מת / שוא'. נַעֲלָמִים is a Niphal participle of ע-ל-מ 'hide'. Ibn Ezra records a second view (from עלם, 'youth', a lover of mockery) which I did not follow; I cite him only for the 'hidden' derivation.

agent_notes: Ibn Ezra removed from the sources of the קְהַל מְרֵעִים note; it is now a lexical note of my own. The commentary now points to the 'assemblies (makhelim) of verse 12, from the same root', not to qahal there.

(PS.26.5 Ibn Ezra: "כי מתי שוא הם בדבור והרשעים במעשה"; PS.26.12: "בְּמַקְהֵלִים אֲבָרֵךְ יְהוָה".)

[consider] Consider softening the KJV audit: 'so' is a defensible reading of the ו, as Radak's 'when ... then' shows. (PS.26.6 Radak: "וכשארחץ בנקיון כפי אז אסבבה את מזבחך" (when I wash ... then I will go around).)

agent_notes: בְּקוֹל is 'with a voice of' (the preposition bet), as in the word table and YLT 'with a voice of'; the earlier gloss dropped it. לַשְׁמִעַ is an unusual Hiphil infinitive without the expected ה; Rashi, Ibn Ezra and Radak all read it as לְהַשְׁמִיעַ, citing Isa 23:11. I follow them.

history.note: [should_fix] Gloss word 2 as 'with a voice of' and make the literal 'to make heard with a voice of thanksgiving' (or 'to sound with a voice of thanksgiving', as YLT). (PS.26.7: "לַשְׁמִעַ בְּקוֹל תּוֹדָה"; word table: "בְּק֣וֹל | HR/Ncmsc | <in> a sound of"; KJV "publish with the voice of thanksgiving".)

agent_notes: The verb אסף 'gather' is used for being gathered to one's people in death (Gen 25:8); Radak, Meiri and Metzudat Zion read it as death. The literal layer keeps the verb; the death sense is brought out in the commentary and the dramatic layer, where it is an implication. נפש is the living self in most of the Bible, but Radak and Meiri read it here as the soul's fate after death; I give both views and choose neither as the only one. STEPBible glosses נפשי 'life my' and חיי 'life my' alike; I kept 'my soul' and 'my life' to show the pair.
